# Add an opt-in spawn animation to menus, keyed on the aligner's zone

## Context

Operator, 2026-08-29, after the menu dismissal work landed (#17850) and while the separator/disabled leaf (#17851) was in review:

> *"if a scroll changes alignments, it would not be a deal-breaker, if that has no animations. cherry on top. we have global css, and the main thread side could even add css selectors which indicate spawn directions, if not already there. then our menu list css could use them, in case the new config is set."*

The refinement that shaped it: a submenu spawning to the right should **slide in from the left** while fading up — directional, not a scale — because the movement reads as the child emerging from its parent.

**Almost every piece already exists.** This ticket is mostly wiring, and the design work was establishing that.

`Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-08-29T19:16Z; no equivalent found.` Closed-issue sweep across `menu animation` / `spawn animation` / `useAnimations menu` / `menu transition`: no declined predecessor — **but see #5008 below, which the closed sweep surfaced and which changes this ticket's naming.** A2A in-flight claim sweep (12 messages, all read-states): no overlapping claim.

## The Problem

A floating menu appears instantly at its resolved position. That is correct and fast, and it should stay the default — but it gives the user no cue about **where the menu came from**, which matters most in a cascade, where a submenu's relationship to its parent item is the entire information the user needs.

The naive implementation fails in three specific ways that are not obvious until you read the main thread, and each one is a real trap rather than a style preference:

1. **Animating the root's `transform` fights the aligner.** `main/DomAccess.mjs:277-280` positions every aligned node with `{top: 0, left: 0, transform: translate(x, y)}`. A spawn `translateX` on the same node either clobbers placement or is clobbered by the next align.
2. **Animating size feeds a re-align loop.** `addAligned()` (`DomAccess.mjs:147-153`) attaches a `ResizeObserver` to the **subject itself** with `syncAligns` as the callback. A scale/height animation changes the observed box → re-align *during* the animation → which re-measures a moving rect, since `getBoundingClientRect()` returns post-transform visual geometry (documented at `DomAccess.mjs:486-491`).
3. **Keying the animation on mount animates before the direction is known.** `component/Base.mjs:622` fires `me.alignTo()` on mount **without awaiting it** — so the node enters the DOM first and the zone is resolved a worker→main round-trip later. There is no anti-flash gate over that window.

## The Architectural Reality

**The direction signal already exists, is already correct, and is already consumed.**

`util/Rectangle.mjs` runs a zone search — candidate zones are tried until one constrains (`:530-560`) — and stamps the resolved side onto the result:

```js
solution.zone = zone;  solution.position = zoneNames[zone];   // ['top','right','bottom','left']
```

`finishAlignResult` (`:73-85`) exists specifically to preserve `zone`/`position` across the offset move. Main then writes it to the DOM:

```js
subject.classList.add(`neo-aligned-${result.position}`);      // DomAccess.mjs:292
```

It is **correctly lifecycle-managed** — the previous position is removed before a re-align (`:243`) and on teardown (`:1287`) — and `resources/scss/src/component/Base.scss` already consumes all four classes to place the box shadow at the correct edge. **Directional spawn is a second consumer of a maintained signal, not a new mechanism.** Because the aligner *flips* when space is short, the animation direction follows the flip for free.

**The spawn-vs-resync distinction also already exists.** `addAligned()` branches on `if (!aligns.has(id))` (`:151`) and marks the id seen at `:189`; `syncAligns()` runs `_aligns.delete(align.id)` once the subject is detached. So first-align, re-align and dismissal are already three distinct, correct moments — and a **reused** menu instance (the pattern `examples/menu/context/` deliberately uses) passes through the delete on dismissal and re-arms as a genuine first-align on reopen.

**Durations are already a governed vocabulary.** `resources/scss/_motion.scss` declares itself *"the ONLY sanctioned duration/easing source"* and states **"a call-site duration/easing literal is a contract violation"**. It supplies `--motion-base: 200ms`, `--motion-panel: 280ms`, `--ease-out-soft`, `--motion-stagger: 24ms`, and collapses every duration to `0ms` under `prefers-reduced-motion` **at the vocabulary level** — so consuming the tokens inherits the accessibility contract instead of re-implementing it.

**Navigation is unaffected by an opacity/transform entrance.** `addon/Navigator.mjs:272` filters with `node.offsetParent && node.matches(selector)`; an element at `opacity: 0` keeps its `offsetParent`, so it stays navigable throughout. (An entrance built on `display`/`visibility` would break arrow-key navigation — recorded as a trap below.)

### Naming — and the prior ruling the closed sweep surfaced

**#5008** (CLOSED/COMPLETED, *"dialog.Base: maximise is no longer animated"*) carries an operator design note:

> *"the dialog should get a new config called `animate_`. `animateTargetId` is still needed for **spawn animations**, but a more generic config to enable / disable all animations seems reasonable. `afterSetAnimate()` should add a new top level CSS rule like `neo-animated`."*

Two consequences:

- **"spawn animation" is the codebase's own term** for this concept — `dialog/Base.mjs:37` still declares `animateTargetId_` for exactly it. The proposed config name should use that word rather than inventing a synonym.
- **`list.Base` already has `animate_`** (`src/list/Base.mjs:27`, reactive, default `false`) — so `menu.List` *inherits it today*. It must **not** be overloaded: `afterSetAnimate()` (`:219`) lazy-imports `list/plugin/Animate.mjs`, which drives **item motion within the list** (reordering/insertion) and marks the owner `neo-animated-list`. Entrance-of-a-floating-surface and motion-of-items-inside-it are different concepts — the latter is the store-re-sort transition seen on the Fleet Manager's 3x3 agent cards, where items glide to new positions in a list that is already on screen.

The nearest sibling (`animate_`) is **reactive**, which settles the reactivity question against the more distant `useAnimations` precedent in `component/DateSelector`, `date/SelectorContainer` and `calendar/view/YearComponent` (all non-reactive, all a different family).

## The Fix

**1. `main/DomAccess.mjs` — make an unchanged alignment idempotent.** Swap the `neo-aligned-*` class only when the subject does not already carry the resolved one, guarded on the SUBJECT rather than the cached align record. A resync then leaves the class — and anything keyed on it — untouched, while a real flip still changes it. No new class, no new state, no new observer.

**2. `src/menu/List.mjs` — the opt-in config.** `animateSpawn_: false`, reactive, whose `afterSet` toggles a root class (proposed `neo-animate-spawn`). Inherited `animate_` is untouched.

**4. `resources/scss/src/menu/List.scss` — four keyframe rules** keyed on the class conjunction, consuming `--motion-*` tokens only:

```scss
.neo-menu-list.neo-animate-spawn.neo-aligned-right { animation-name: neo-menu-spawn-from-left; }
```

Nothing is added to the theme sheets: this is geometry and motion, and motion is mode-invariant by `_motion.scss`'s own design.

## Corrections from implementation (PR #17861)

Two prescriptions in **The Fix** were wrong and are struck rather than silently rewritten — the reasoning that killed them is the useful part.

**~~An inner wrapper node~~ is not needed.** The premise was that the animation could not share the root with the aligner's `transform`. It can: the individual `translate` property **composes** with `transform` rather than clobbering it. Measured — `transform: translate(300px,200px)` plus `translate: -40px 0` resolves to `x = 260` with the matrix intact, and the codebase already uses the individual property in 7 places. No structural change to the vdom.

> ⚠️ **The paragraph below is itself superseded by Correction 2** — it names `unalign()`, which does not
> exist, and rests on *"a same-zone resync leaves `animation-name` untouched"*, which was falsified at
> runtime. Kept only as the reasoning trail; **nothing in it describes what shipped.**

**~~Remove the marker on the first `syncAligns`~~ — that cancels the entrance.** `onDocumentMutation` resyncs *every* aligned subject on ordinary body churn, and opening a submenu is enough to trigger it, so a per-align removal strips the marker milliseconds in and the animation dies. It is cleared by `unalign()` instead. Safe because a resync that keeps the same zone leaves `animation-name` untouched, and an unchanged name does not restart a running animation (measured: an animation kept advancing across unrelated class churn, 583ms → 1583ms, and reset to 0 only when the name changed). A genuine zone flip replays, which the operator accepted up front.

**One addition the ticket did not name:** `showSubMenu()` must propagate the config. Without it the cascade stays still while only the root animates — inverting the effect the feature exists for. Both this and the marker defect passed review-by-reading and were caught only in the browser.

## Correction 2 — the marker is gone (PR #17861 review, RA-1/RA-3)

**~~`neo-align-initial`~~ does not exist and should not.** The design above rested on *"a resync that keeps the same zone leaves `animation-name` untouched, so a running animation is not restarted."* @neo-gpt falsified it at runtime and I reproduced it: `align()` **removes** the zone class, reads layout, then re-adds it — `currentTime` 949ms → `animation-name: none` with zero animations → a **different** `Animation` object at 0. The final name is identical throughout, which is precisely why a name-only assertion passes while the entrance restarts.

**The fix moved to the root:** `align()` swaps the zone class only when the subject does not already carry it. An ordinary resync leaves the class — and the running animation, and the shadow repaint — untouched; a real flip still changes it and restarts the entrance mirrored. The transient marker is deleted, which also retires the claim that the default path was byte-unchanged: nothing is added to every aligned subject any more.

**The guard is on the SUBJECT, not the cached align record.** Keying off `lastAlign` looks equivalent and is not — a hidden menu leaves the DOM and remounts classless while `_aligns` still reports the same zone, so that version never re-added the class and a reused menu stayed unaligned permanently. Caught by the reuse witness one run after writing it.

**`unalign()` does not exist.** I named it as the cleanup authority in code comments, the PR body and this ticket. The cleanup lives in `syncAligns()`. Corrected everywhere.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — aligned-with `_motion.scss`'s stated vocabulary authority; no ADR interaction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `main/DomAccess.mjs` leaves the `neo-aligned-*` class untouched when a resync resolves the same zone, and swaps it on a real flip — witnessed by WAAPI animation identity and monotonic progress, not by the resolved `animation-name`, which is identical across a restart.
- [ ] `menu.List#animateSpawn_` defaults `false`; with the default, the rendered DOM and computed styles are **unchanged from today** — asserted, not assumed.
- [ ] With `animateSpawn: true`, a submenu resolving to zone `right` has computed `animation-name` of the from-the-left keyframes; zone `left` resolves to the mirrored keyframes. No wrapper node: the individual `translate` property composes with the aligner-owned `transform`.
- [ ] **The flip case:** a submenu opened near the right viewport edge resolves `neo-aligned-left` and its animation mirrors accordingly — the case that is painful to hand-code and silent when broken.
- [ ] **A later `animateSpawn` change reaches already-cached submenus in BOTH directions** — `showSubMenu()` copies the value at creation only, so a reused submenu would otherwise stay stale.
- [ ] Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (Playwright `emulateMedia`), the resolved animation duration is `0s` — exercising the `_motion.scss` collapse rather than trusting it.
- [ ] No duration or easing literal appears in `menu/List.scss`; every value resolves through a `--motion-*` token.
- [ ] Arrow-key navigation reaches every item **during** the entrance window (guards against a `display`/`visibility` implementation, which would drop items from `Navigator`'s `offsetParent` filter).
- [ ] Coverage lives in the component tier (`test/playwright/component/menu/`), which drives real pointer input in a real browser. Assertions are on the **class/`animation-name` contract**, never on a sampled visual mid-animation state, and the `animateSpawn: false` arm is verified able to fail.

## Out of Scope

- **Exit / dismissal animation.** Deliberate, and the reason is specific: dismissal now cascades `unmount()` through the whole tree from three entry points (leaf click, outside pointer, Escape), and that cascade was regressed as recently as #17850. Animating exits means deferring DOM removal until the animation ends, which opens a window where a menu is visibly present but logically dismissed — and would invalidate the `[3, 0]` level-count witness added in PR #17852. Its own ticket, after the cascade has mileage.
- **Any other floating surface** (dialog, picker, tooltip). If this shape proves out, generalising it to `component.Base` is a follow-up — but a generic config is not justified by one consumer.
- **Per-item entrance stagger.** `--motion-stagger` exists and menus are short enough to use it, but it is a separate visual decision.
- **Changing `neo-aligned-*` semantics or the zone search.** Read-only inputs here.

## Avoided Traps

- **Do not reuse `list.Base#animate_`.** It is inherited and available, and it means something else entirely. Operator's example, 2026-08-29: *"think of fleet manager agent cards => 3x3. we re-sort the store, and items transition to their new positions."* That is **items moving between positions inside a settled list**; this ticket is **a floating surface arriving**. One flag for both would load `list/plugin/Animate.mjs` into every menu that only wanted a fade, and would make "animate this menu" ambiguous between two unrelated behaviours.
- **Do not animate the menu root's `transform`.** It is the aligner's positioning channel (`DomAccess.mjs:280`).
- **Do not animate anything that changes the root's layout box.** The `ResizeObserver` at `DomAccess.mjs:153` observes the subject and re-aligns on change — this is the mechanical reason a slide is correct and a scale is not.
- **Do not key the entrance on mount.** The zone is not known yet (`component/Base.mjs:622` does not await `alignTo`).
- **Do not write `200ms` anywhere.** `_motion.scss` names that a contract violation, and the token carries the reduced-motion collapse.

- 2026-08-29T21:28:36Z @tobiu referenced in commit `8f466ba` - "feat(menu): an opt-in entrance that follows the side the aligner chose (#17860) (#17861)

* feat(menu): an opt-in entrance that follows the side the aligner chose (#17860)

`menu.List#animateSpawn` (default false) fades a menu up while sliding it in
from the side it spawned on, so a submenu reads as emerging from the item that
opened it.

The direction is never configured. `DomAccess.align()` already publishes the
side the zone search settled on as `neo-aligned-{top|right|bottom|left}` -- it
has done since the box-shadow edge needed it -- so the entrance reads the
outcome instead of guessing, and mirrors for free when the search FLIPS a
submenu for want of space. That flip is the case a configured direction always
gets wrong.

What is new on the main thread is one marker. `addAligned()` already branched on
`!aligns.has(id)` to install its observers; that branch is the subject's arrival
rather than a resync, so it now also adds `neo-align-initial`. CSS cannot
otherwise tell the two apart -- both produce a `neo-aligned-*` change.

Three constraints shaped the implementation, each measured rather than assumed:

- The entrance animates the individual `translate` property, not `transform`.
  The aligner owns `transform` (it writes `translate(x,y)` there to position the
  menu) and the two compose: `transform: translate(300px,200px)` plus
  `translate: -40px 0` lands at x=260 with the matrix intact. No wrapper node is
  needed, which is what the ticket originally proposed.
- Nothing that changes the layout box may animate. `addAligned()` observes the
  subject with a ResizeObserver and re-aligns on size change, so a scale or
  height entrance would re-enter alignment mid-flight and measure its own motion.
- The marker is cleared by `unalign()` and NOT per-align. Per-align looks like
  the tighter contract and is wrong: `onDocumentMutation` resyncs every aligned
  subject on ordinary body churn -- opening a submenu is enough -- which stripped
  the marker milliseconds into the entrance and cancelled it. Live verification
  caught that; the spec now pins it. Leaving the marker until dismissal is safe
  because a resync keeping the same zone leaves `animation-name` untouched, and
  an unchanged name does not restart a running animation (measured: an animation
  kept advancing across unrelated class churn, and reset to 0 only when the name
  changed).

`showSubMenu()` propagates the config, since a cascade whose children stayed
still while the root moved would invert the effect the feature exists for --
also caught by live verification, not by reading.

Durations and easings come from `_motion.scss`, which names a call-site literal a
contract violation and collapses every tier to 0ms under `prefers-reduced-motion`
-- so the accessibility contract is inherited rather than reimplemented.

Deliberately not included: exit animation. Dismissal cascades `unmount()` through
the tree from three entry points, that cascade regressed as recently as #17850,
and deferring DOM removal would open a dismissed-but-visible window and
invalidate the level-count witness from #17852.
